correctness.rationale: Starting from Proposition 5 of arXiv:2604.04747, the exact Bernoulli-refresh transition probabilities yield stationary p-binomial counts and a stationary OU functional CLT on n-step windows. The sink count at the deterministic center has an independent Gaussian fluctuation; a maximal binomial-refresh martingale bound and Doob control of the sink count exclude early crossings, while an endpoint Gaussian bound controls late crossings. OU paths immediately cross C1 moving boundaries, making the first-contact map valid. Conditioning on the Gaussian intercept and using OU stationarity/reversibility produces the stated drift-penalized OU supremum. The packaged Python checker passed 69,812 exact finite assertions, but it is not a proof of weak convergence.

Identifying the fixed-constant window with a universal stationary OU supremum, proving cancellation of the random sink-clock intercept, and deriving strict monotone comparisons and both endpoints supplies a motivated quantitative law, not an arbitrary parameter substitution or a previously tabulated constant.
